text:
sarah: Anyone else seeing the inference-frontend svc in eu-west stop resolving briefly after the spot GPU pool scaled down? Apps get 503s and `dig` shows NXDOMAIN for frontend.svc.cluster.local for ~20-40s :eyes:

ben: Which nodes were drained? can you grab `kubectl get endpoints` + `kubectl get endpointslice` for the service when it happens?

sarah: quick snippet I grabbed when it flapped:```
$ kubectl get endpoints frontend -o wide
NAME       ENDPOINTS        AGE
frontend   10.10.5.23:80    3m
```then it flips to `<none>` for ~30s and the LB healthchecks fail

priya: saw similar in logs — node-spot-23 got preempted, pods moved, and kube-proxy on the target node restarted. conntrack entries for pod IPs got dropped, coredns had positive A records cached, clients tried the old pod IPs -> 503s. Our LB probes go direct to pod IPs so they fail fast.

infra-bot: [alert] node-spot-23 preempted at 2024-06-14T17:02:31Z; 48 pods rescheduled. kube-proxy restarted on node-spot-42.

ben: short-term options: rollout-restart coredns in the cluster after a large scale-down (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n kube-system`), or restart kube-proxy DS selectively. also consider raising conntrack table/timeouts on kube-proxy. Not ideal but reduces flap window.

sarah: doing the coredns restart in eu-west now. tagging @oncall to watch for recurrence. I'll also drain more gracefully (cordon -> wait for endpointslice update -> evict) for the next batch.

priya: adding to runbook: when spot GPU pool scales down, run a coredns cache flush + check kube-proxy conntrack metrics in the target AZ. long-term: make drain sequence wait for endpoint slice reconciliation and add a pre-drain hook to quiesce LB traffic. :thumbsup:

ben: +1
